title: Restriction to an open intersection detects isomorphisms between open direct images
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let O,P,W be opens with W = O ∩ P, and fix derived module categories on X,O,P,W with one morphism universe [def-pc-derived-category]. Write rO and rW for canonical exact derived restriction [def-pc-derived-open-restriction-maps], and JP = RjP_*, JW = RjW_* for derived direct images [def-pc-derived-direct-image]. For any B in D(P), C in D(W) and morphism f : JP(B) → JW(C), if rW(f) is an isomorphism then rO(f) is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 08FE (lemma-restrict-direct-image-open), used in the local identification of Tag 08DG (lemma-glue)

proof.text: Let iO : W → O be the inclusion. Scheme.Modules.overMapCompOverEquiv and the over-equivalence counit identify transported overlap restriction with restriction along k = X.homOfLE(leOfHom iO). Transport Scheme.Modules.restrictAdjunction k along this isomorphism and derive it using Adjunction.mapDerivedCategoryRightDerivedAdjunction, giving L ⊣ Rk_*. Underived open direct image is fully faithful by its invertible counit and preserves K-injectives because L is exact; the source-library full_rightDerivedFunctor and faithful_rightDerivedFunctor instances give full faithfulness of Rk_*.

source.place: Tag 08FE (lemma-restrict-direct-image-open), used in the local identification of Tag 08DG (lemma-glue)

proof.text: Apply the essential-image theorem to P,W and then to W,W. The second application is valid since W ≤ O and hence W = O ∩ W. Both rO(JP B) and rO(JW C) lie in the essential image of Rk_*.

source.place: Tag 08FE (lemma-restrict-direct-image-open), used in the local identification of Tag 08DG (lemma-glue)

proof.text: The adjunction unit at both objects is invertible by Adjunction.isIso_unit_app_iff_mem_essImage. The canonical derived nested-restriction comparison transports the hypothesis IsIso(rW(f)) into IsIso(L(rO(f))). Naturality of the unit expresses rO(f) followed by its target unit as its source unit followed by Rk_*(L(rO(f))). All factors on the latter side are invertible, so cancel the target unit to prove IsIso(rO(f)).

theorem derived_open_intersection_isIso_of_restriction
    (X : Scheme.{u}) (O P W : X.Opens) (hW : W = O ⊓ P)
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings O.toScheme.toRingedSpace))]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings P.toScheme.toRingedSpace))]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings W.toScheme.toRingedSpace))]
    (B : schemeDerivedCategory P.toScheme) (C : schemeDerivedCategory W.toScheme)
    (f : (schemeDerivedDirectImage P.ι).obj B ⟶ (schemeDerivedDirectImage W.ι).obj C)
    (hf : IsIso ((schemeOpenRestriction X W).mapDerivedCategory.map f)) :
    IsIso ((schemeOpenRestriction X O).mapDerivedCategory.map f)
